prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional ATFM+A-CDM; airports Meridian International(=Meridian Regional Airport), Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport. Modes (Airport Duty Manager=ADM declares; Business Rules Registry holds thresholds, connection protection, gate/towing/stand rules, materiality, and border/customs states: blocking, human-confirm, informational): Normal; Adverse Weather (tighter escalation; ADM may cut remote stands); Capacity Reduction State(extended metering); Recovery Phase(Copperfin-approved; RFM authorizes exit); Contingency Fallback(Contingency Operations Console); Slot Compliance; Winter(MBO confirms). Actors: Regional Flow Manager=RFM(ranks diversions; uses remote stand delays and aggregated border delay exposure to adjust arrival regulation vs local absorption), Airspace Sector Planner, Military Airspace Liaison, Tower Supervisor, ADM(Medical Diversion Notice; Customs Hold Release Note), Ramp Control Lead(uses Towbar Shortage Report), Ground Handling Dispatcher=GHD(produces Towbar Shortage Report), Aircraft Operator Rep, Airline Operations Coordinator(TOBT revision requests; uses customs hold visibility for connections/messaging/turnaround), Slot Coordinator, Network Operations Liaison, Emergency Response Coordinator, Deicing Coordinator, Meteorology Briefing Officer=MBO, Data Governance Steward. Cedarbell=Regional Flow Platform(flight border release readiness attribute). Parts: Marlinstone=Demand Prediction Service(unknown border status→uncertain turnaround); CAM=Capacity Assessment Module(remote stand limits, persistent apron congestion reduce throughput, Normal/Adverse); Arrival Regulation Console(uses Medical Diversion Notice for arrival priority/stand/border); Blueharbor=Slot Allocation Engine(CTT=Calculated Takeoff Time, GDP, Pushback Window Token; no aggressive slot under unresolved customs hold); Foxglove=Airport CDM Portal(Collaborative Decision Log; remote stand records; controlled border/customs view for authorized users); Common Situation Display; Emberline=Departure Metering Service(CTT→Ironleaf=Tower Sequence Manager; considers confirmed apron blockage, remote stand release); Nightjar; Halcyon; Runway Meters; Surface Surveillance Adapter(normalizes apron data into movement/occupancy/blockage events); East Apron Sensor(occupancy transitions, lane blockage durations, confidence, synced time); West Apron Sensor(verifies remote stand/service road availability); Ramp Movement Board(apron evidence for stand release/taxi lane/vehicle conflict); Gate Conflict Detector(border+apron evidence: true conflict vs clearance

New part:
S587: The Data Governance Steward maintains the access rules and retention rules for border and customs data because the data can affect both operational outcomes and passenger privacy obligations.
S588: The Alert Distribution Hub issues targeted alerts when a customs hold conflicts with an assigned stand plan or when apron sensing contradicts a declared off-block milestone.
S589: The Collaborative Decision Log records the operational reason when border release status, customs hold status, or apron sensing data changes a sequencing or stand allocation decision.
S590: The Performance Analytics Warehouse compares planned clearance assumptions with actual border release timing and apron availability to improve future demand prediction and resource planning.
S591: The airport-level constraint process starts by translating en-route demand indicators into rates, time windows, and advisories that can be understood by local operations teams.
S592: Each Sector Load Monitor supplies time-bucketed counts, predicted occupancy, and overload flags for the sectors that feed or constrain Meridian arrivals and departures.
S593: The Regional Flow Platform aligns these sector values with scheduled movements from Flight Data Exchange and predicted readiness from Demand Prediction Service.
S594: When a sector is predicted to exceed its planning threshold, Capacity Assessment Module evaluates whether the affected traffic is dominated by departures, arrivals, or mixed flows.
S595: For departure-dominated overload, the conversion result is normally an airport departure rate, a constrained departure fix allocation, or a proposed spacing value at the runway release point.
S596: For arrival-dominated overload, the result is expressed as an adjusted Airport Acceptance Rate or a metered arrival stream for Arrival Regulation Console.
S597: Mixed-flow constraints are converted into paired measures so that departure metering does not protect one sector by creating an unmanaged arrival queue.
S598: The Regional Flow Manager uses the load sheet to confirm whether a departure fix constraint should be represented as an airport departure measure.
S599: Departure fix saturation is calculated by comparing planned departures by fix against the usable fix capacity declared in Airport Capacity Plan.
S600: Capacity Assessment Module applies Business Rules Registry thresholds to distinguish a short tactical peak from sustained saturation requiring a Tactical Regulation Proposal.
S601: A short peak normally becomes a sequence advisory in Tower Sequence Manager or a limited departure metering adjustment in Departure Metering Service.
S602: Sustained saturation is converted into revised Calculated Takeoff Time targets and, when necessary, adjusted Target Off Block Time values published through Airport CDM Portal.
S603: The Slot Allocation Engine preserves equity by distributing delay across operators according to the active Ground Delay Program logic and local priority rules.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
